items.title: Friends of the liver: Punjab’s quiet epidemic of male heartbreak
items.summary: In Punjab, a pair of lifelong best friends are called jigri yaar : friends joined not merely at the heart but at the liver. The phrase suggests an intimacy so deep it is almost anatomical, as if friendship has passed beyond feeling and entered the body. Punjabi songs and Hindi films have long celebrated this kind of male devotion: two men eating from the same plate, sleeping under the same quilt, risking death for each other, calling each other brother because no other word is available. What these stories rarely make room for is what happens when one of those men leaves. For those of us who came of age in the 1990s, before terms like gay, lesbian, and bisexual entered our vocabulary, these portrayals of fraternal love provided rare openings. They allowed us to expand our suppressed desires into the realm of fantasy. Queer philosopher Judith Butler has argued that fantasy is not the opposite of reality but rather shaped by it, filling in what reality so frequently denies.
